content.title: About
content.content: Baby toddler cereal is a ready‑to‑eat oatmeal product specially formulated for children from 6 months old. It is fortified with vitamins and minerals, has a mild flavor and a soft texture that eases the transition to solid foods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat flakes provide soluble fiber that supports a healthy gut microbiome.
The product is typically free of added sugar, making it suitable for early nutrition.
Cereals are often fortified with iron and vitamin D, essential for bone growth in children.
Ready‑to‑eat format is convenient – just add warm water or milk.
Oats are considered a low‑allergy grain, though a wheat‑free label should be checked if the child has celiac disease.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Soluble fiber in oats helps soften stools and prevents constipation in infants.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Fortified iron aids in preventing iron‑deficiency anemia during rapid growth periods.

items.title: Vitamin D for bones
items.content: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption, promoting healthy skeletal development.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: Absence of added sugar helps establish healthy taste preferences early on.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to oats; any signs of reaction should be evaluated by a pediatrician.

items.title: Gluten cross‑contamination
items.content: Oats are often processed on equipment that also handles wheat, so trace gluten may be present.

items.title: Over‑consumption
items.content: Excessive portions can lead to unnecessary calorie intake; follow serving size recommendations.

items.title: Serving temperature
items.content: Serve the cereal warm, not hot, to avoid burns in the mouth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix the cereal with warm water, breast milk, or formula to the desired consistency. For variety, stir in fruit or vegetable puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, reseal tightly and use within 4–6 weeks.

cheese-cottage-cheese-with-gelatin-desse.title: Cottage Cheese with Gelatin Dessert and Vegetables

content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese with gelatin dessert and vegetables is a ready‑to‑eat dish that combines soft cottage cheese, gelatin‑based jelly, and fresh vegetables. The mix of protein, light sweetness and crunchy veggies makes it a convenient option for breakfast, a snack, or a light dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is a traditional dairy product in many Eastern European cuisines.
Gelatin jelly is often used in culinary arts to add a delicate texture and visual contrast.
Combining cottage cheese with vegetables boosts the nutritional profile with added vitamins and minerals.
The dish is easy to pack in single‑serve containers, making it popular in school cafeterias and office lunch boxes.
Variations may include carrots, cucumbers, bell peppers, tomatoes, or other seasonal vegetables.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality dairy protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone health and proper nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat (when using low‑fat varieties)
items.content: Choosing low‑fat cottage cheese keeps the dish light and suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals from vegetables
items.content: Vegetables add vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium, and dietary fiber, promoting good digestion.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The gelatin dessert is mostly water, helping to maintain proper hydration.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cottage cheese contains lactose; people with intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Gelatin is derived from animal collagen and may cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some ready‑made versions may contain added salt; those with hypertension should check the label.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Both cottage cheese and fresh vegetables spoil quickly; keep refrigerated and consume within 2‑3 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be enjoyed as a snack, paired with whole‑grain bread, or used as a filling for wraps. For extra flavor, sprinkle fresh herbs or drizzle a little olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C in the original packaging. Once opened, consume within 48 hours. Discard if you notice sour odor or discoloration.

content.title: About
content.content: Chewing gum, sugar free (5125) is a low‑calorie product designed to freshen breath and satisfy the urge to chew without added sugar. It contains sugar substitutes such as xylitol or sorbitol, plus flavorings and menthol for long‑lasting freshness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sugar‑free gum is often used in dentistry to reduce caries risk because xylitol inhibits bacterial growth.
The first commercial sugar‑free gum appeared in the 1970s.
Some versions are fortified with vitamin C or other additives for extra oral care benefits.
Chewing gum stimulates saliva flow, which helps neutralize acids in the mouth.
Menthol enhances the feeling of freshness and can ease breathing during a cold.

items.title: Reduced caries risk
items.content: Xylitol, commonly used in sugar‑free gums, suppresses cariogenic bacteria and promotes enamel remineralization.

items.title: Improved oral hygiene
items.content: Increased saliva production helps wash away food debris and neutralize acids.

items.title: Weight control
items.content: Low‑calorie gum can replace higher‑calorie sweets, aiding energy intake management.

items.title: Breath freshness
items.content: Menthol and flavor agents provide lasting fresh breath without sugar.

items.title: Support for dental work
items.content: Absence of sugar reduces the risk of damage to fillings and prosthetics.

items.title: Allergy to sugar substitutes
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to xylitol or sorbitol, experiencing gastrointestinal upset.

items.title: Digestive issues
items.content: Large amounts of sugar substitutes can cause gas, diarrhea, or bloating.

items.title: Not for children under 3
items.content: Chewing gum poses a choking hazard for young children.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Xylitol may affect blood sugar levels in diabetics; consult a healthcare professional.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chew the gum for 5‑10 minutes after meals or whenever you need fresh breath. Do not swallow; discard the gum after chewing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed to prevent drying out. For extended shelf life, keep in the refrigerator.

chicken-leg-drumstick-and-thigh-grilled-.title: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh, grilled with sauce, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh are dark‑meat cuts that are rich in flavor and nutrients. Grilled with sauce and the skin left on, they develop a crispy crust and juicy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark meat contains more iron and zinc than white meat.
Grilling imparts a smoky aroma that enhances taste perception.
Chicken skin is a notable source of beneficial fats, including monounsaturated fatty acids.
Common sauces often combine honey, soy sauce, garlic and spices, adding antioxidant compounds.
These preparations are staples in American barbecue and many Asian cuisines.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken leg, drumstick and thigh provide about 20‑25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Dark meat supplies higher amounts of iron and zinc, essential for immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in vitamin B12, niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6), which aid nerve health and energy metabolism.

items.title: Beneficial fats in the skin
items.content: The skin contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Antioxidants from the sauce
items.content: Herbs, spices and a touch of sugar in the sauce add polyphenols with antioxidant activity.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cooking with skin and sauce increases calories and saturated fat intake.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Sauces are often salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C to prevent salmonella.

items.title: Allergy to sauce ingredients
items.content: Some sauces contain soy, mustard or other allergens that can trigger reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main dish, sliced for salads, sandwiches or as a snack. The skin can be eaten if crispy, or removed to lower calorie density.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked portions in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wing, sauteed are pieces of chicken meat quickly cooked in a pan until golden and crisp. They have a juicy flavor, a slightly crunchy texture, and the aroma of typical seasoning used for pan‑frying.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are a popular bar and restaurant snack worldwide.
They are traditionally marinated in a blend of soy sauce, honey, garlic and ginger.
In the US, “Buffalo wings” are famous – wings tossed in a spicy chili‑pepper sauce.
Chicken wings contain more bones than most other chicken parts, making them a fun culinary challenge.
Proper pan‑saute can achieve a crispy crust without deep‑frying.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Wings provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: They supply vitamin B6 and niacin, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Wings contain iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Ideal for low‑carb diets as they contain minimal carbs.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: When sautéed with a modest amount of oil, they retain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared marinades and sauces can add a lot of salt, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Fat from frying
items.content: Using excessive oil can make the dish calorie‑dense and introduce trans fats.

items.title: Risk of undercooking
items.content: Chicken must be fully cooked to prevent food‑borne illnesses such as salmonella.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as an appetizer, add to salads, use in tacos or Asian‑style dishes. Common accompaniments include barbecue sauce, blue‑cheese dip, honey‑mustard, or spicy buffalo sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw wings refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked sautéed wings should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate chip reduced‑fat cookie is a crunchy snack made with whole‑grain flour, a modest amount of vegetable oil, and dark chocolate chips. The lower fat content makes it a lighter alternative to traditional chocolate cookies while preserving a rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Contains about 30 % less fat than regular chocolate cookies.
A small amount of oil and leavening agents are used to keep the cookie crisp.
Chocolate chips are coated with a thin layer of cocoa butter to enhance aroma.
Often included in school lunch programs where calorie balance is important.
Packaging is made from recyclable material meeting environmental standards.

items.title: Reduced Calorie Load
items.content: Lower fat reduces overall calories per serving, supporting weight‑management goals.

items.title: Source of Whole Grains
items.content: Whole‑grain flour provides dietary fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants from Chocolate
items.content: Dark chocolate chips contain flavonoids that may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Low Glycemic Impact
items.content: The combination of whole grains and modest sugar helps avoid sharp blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: B‑Vitamins
items.content: Flour and chocolate supply B1, B2, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Gluten Allergy
items.content: The cookie contains wheat, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Chocolate Allergy
items.content: Cocoa may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar Content
items.content: Although fat is reduced, sugar is still present, so diabetics should monitor portion size.

items.title: Food Additives
items.content: Emulsifiers and leavening agents may cause discomfort for those with a sensitive stomach.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone snack, crumble it into yogurt or granola, or use it in desserts such as ice‑cream toppings. For a softer texture, briefly warm in the microwave (10–15 seconds).

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life (over 3 months) keep refrigerated to maintain crunch and prevent moisture absorption.

content.title: About
content.content: The "Vanilla Sandwich" cookie with extra filling consists of two soft vanilla cookies sandwiched with a creamy flavored filling. An additional layer such as chocolate ganache, caramel, or fruit jam may be added, giving the treat a richer and more varied taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first vanilla sandwich cookie appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a popular school cafeteria snack.
Extra fillings often change with the seasons – berries in spring and spiced caramel in winter.
Vanilla flavor in the cookie is derived from natural vanilla beans or synthetic vanillin, which tastes the same.
The cookie is frequently used in culinary contests as a base for creating new dessert compositions.
The sandwich structure helps keep the filling fresh longer than in regular cookies.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vanilla extract supplies small amounts of vitamin B6, supporting the nervous system.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Unlike salty snacks, this cookie typically contains little added salt.

items.title: Plant‑based oils
items.content: The dough is often made with vegetable oils, which provide essential fatty acids.

items.title: Mood‑boosting
items.content: Sweet taste and vanilla aroma can stimulate serotonin production, improving mood.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: High sugar levels may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The dough usually contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: The filling is often made with butter or milk.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Each sandwich can contain 150–250 kcal, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie is convenient as a standalone snack, can be added to lunchboxes, or used in desserts – for example, crumbled over ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 7 days. For longer storage, keep refrigerated for up to 3 weeks or frozen for up to 3 months.

content.title: About
content.content: The salmon cake or patty (1350) is made from minced salmon fillet formed into small cakes or sticks. It has a delicate pink hue, a characteristic sea‑fish aroma, and a soft, slightly crumbly texture when cooked.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon is one of the most nutrient‑dense fish, rich in omega‑3 fatty acids.
Salmon patties are popular in diet plans because they are low in saturated fat.
Traditional salmon cakes originate from Scandinavian cuisine, where salmon is a staple.
The product can be steamed, baked, or lightly pan‑fried while retaining most nutrients.
Salmon cakes are often served with a dill‑lemon sauce.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Salmon provides EPA and DHA, fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Each patty supplies a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12, B6 and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Salmon offers selenium, phosphorus and potassium, beneficial for immunity and bones.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, salmon patties have a more favorable fat profile.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including salmon.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: While salmon generally has low mercury levels, people with heightened sensitivity should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared patties may contain added salt; those with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Commercial versions can contain preservatives or flavor enhancers that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The patty can be steamed, baked in the oven, or lightly pan‑fried. Serve it with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, rice, or a fresh salad. It pairs well with a yogurt‑dill‑lemon sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the patties in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze them at –18 °C; they retain quality for up to 3 months. Discard any that develop an off‑smell.

infant-formula-similac-sensitive-powder-.title: Infant formula, Similac Sensitive, powder, prepared with baby water

content.title: About
content.content: Similac Sensitive is a powdered infant formula designed for babies with a sensitive digestive system. It contains partially hydrolyzed protein, prebiotics, and an optimal blend of vitamins and minerals to support growth and development. Preparation with specially filtered baby water adds an extra level of purity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The formula uses partially hydrolyzed casein, making it easier to digest for sensitive infants.
Includes prebiotic fibers (FOS) that promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Clinically tested to confirm its hypoallergenic properties.
Available in 400 g cans, providing several weeks of feeding.
Preparation recommends using filtered water to minimize contamination risk.

items.title: Supports growth and development
items.content: A balanced mix of vitamins and minerals (including iron, zinc, vitamin D) supports bone growth and nervous system development.

items.title: Easy digestion
items.content: Partially hydrolyzed protein reduces digestive load and lowers the chance of allergic reactions.

items.title: Gut microbiome support
items.content: Prebiotics stimulate beneficial bacteria, contributing to healthy digestion.

items.title: Helps prevent constipation
items.content: Optimal fiber and probiotic components aid regular bowel movements.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and zinc play key roles in supporting an infant’s immune function.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Despite hydrolysis, some infants may still be sensitive to milk proteins.

items.title: Improper reconstitution
items.content: A solution that is too concentrated can strain the kidneys; follow manufacturer guidelines.

items.title: Water temperature control
items.content: Water that is too hot can degrade certain vitamins; use water at 40‑50 °C.

items.title: Shelf‑life after opening
items.content: Powder can absorb moisture; store in a dry place and use within 30 days of opening.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Measure the recommended amount of powder (typically one scoop per 30 ml of water), add pre‑cooled baby water at room temperature, and mix thoroughly until smooth. Let the mixture sit for 2‑3 minutes before feeding.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, seal tightly to prevent moisture ingress.
